lines.text: There's a window in my bedroom that's tilted sideways. Last night, something outside tilted its head to *match it.*
Old farmhouses in Vermont have them. Witch windows. The legend says a witch can't fly her broom through a crooked window.
The real reason is boring. Builders tilted a normal window to squeeze it in under the roof.
I bought this house last month. My witch window is upstairs, looking out over the dark field behind the barn.
The first night, I heard scratching on the glass. Two floors off the ground.
The second night, I saw it. A long, pale face, pressed against the glass. *Sideways.*
Not like someone peeking in. Tilted at exactly the angle of the window. Like it was trying to *fit.*
I asked the old man who sold me the house about it. He said his family never called it a witch window.
They called it the coffin window. When someone died upstairs, they slid the coffin out through it. Sideways.
So the dead wouldn't know the way back in through the door.
I asked him who died in my bedroom. He said his father. In 1961.
Last night the scratching stopped. I thought it had given up.
Then I heard the window slide open. Slowly. And something long came in... *sideways.*
